title: Ops incident comms — dry run for company update + Q&A
body:
Purpose:
This is a rough draft for the company-wide status update we plan to give at the next all-hands. Focus: short, factual timeline; what we changed; customer impact; and a short Q&A bank so managers can answer questions in teams. NOT final — lots of TODOs and open items below.

Audience: everyone (engineers, product, support, sales, ops, execs). Tone: transparent, accountable, technical-but-accessible.

Headline (one-liner for slides/email):
On March 3–4 we experienced degraded latency for hosted inference due to a cascading autoscaler bug; services are stable now and we’ve deployed mitigations and long-term fixes. No customer data was exposed.

TL;DR (3 bullets):
- Root cause: autoscaler mis-evaluated GPU pool headroom when a set of healthchecks returned transient failures; this caused repeated scale-down/scale-up flapping and cache invalidation across model shards.
- Impact: elevated tail latency for ~2.5 hours for ~18% of requests in us-west and eu-west regions; several customers reported timeouts.
- Status: immediate mitigations deployed (disable aggressive downscaler + sticky cache pinning), incident closed at 2026-03-04 11:30 PT; long-term fix in RFC and scheduled for next sprint.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-03 07:12 PT — first alert: elevated 95/99th latency in us-west serving pool
- 2026-03-03 07:18 PT — SRE oncall begins investigation; see JIRA-OPS-9876
- 2026-03-03 07:42 PT — identified pattern: rapid scale downs following transient HC failures; cache eviction observed in logs
- 2026-03-03 08:05 PT — mitigation: temporarily disabled aggressive autoscaler policy for affected pools
- 2026-03-03 09:00 PT — partial recovery; latency improved but remained noisy due to warmed/unwarmed KV cache states
- 2026-03-03 11:30 PT — final mitigation: enabled sticky cache pinning + conservative downscale rules; system stabilized

What we did (operational summary):
- Short-term: disabled the downscale trigger threshold and increased healthcheck patience; forced warm-up of critical model shards; communicated to support and customer success with template messages.
- Mid-term: introduced cache pinning for top N shards to reduce churn on scale events; added a circuit-breaker to prevent rolling down below baseline capacity.
- Long-term: RFC (link above) proposes autoscaler rewrite to incorporate rolling health windows and token-based quota awareness; plan includes e2e integration tests and a chaos regression job. Target: rollout in 2 sprints.

Customer impact and outreach:
- Impact: intermittent timeouts, increased latency for a subset of inference requests. Internal metric: 18% requests hit >99th latency spike for ~2.5 hours in two regions. No data exfiltration.
- Outreach: CS sent initial notices to impacted accounts; we offered credits to customers who logged severity incidents. Support ticket template is in the linked Confluence doc.

What we learned (lessons):
- Autoscaler heuristics need a safety floor for capacity and be aware of cold-cache cost; scale-to-zero patterns were too aggressive for the current workload distribution.
- Observability gaps: we need a clear metric showing cache hotness per shard (not just pool-level hit rate).
- Playbooks: incident runbook lacked a quick step to pin critical shards; adding that reduces MTTR.

Speaking notes for all-hands (bullet phrases):
- "We hit an availability hiccup earlier this month; I want to walk through what happened and what we’re doing to prevent this from happening again."
- "Importantly: no customer data was exposed — the issue was operational behavior around scaling and cache warming."
- "We owned this quickly: SRE contained the problem, CS proactively contacted impacted customers, and we shipped mitigations the same day."
- "Next: a small set of engineering changes (autoscaler fixes, cache pinning) plus new monitoring and tests to keep this from recurring."

Anticipated questions + draft answers (Q&A bank):
Q: Was customer data compromised?
A: Short answer: no. We reviewed logs and access patterns; there’s no evidence of data leakage. The issue affected request latency and availability only.

Q: How many customers were affected?
A: Roughly 12 customers reported incidents during the window; our telemetry shows ~18% of requests in two regions experienced latency spikes. We proactively reached out to any account with >1% error increase.

Q: What is the timeline for a permanent fix?
A: RFC posted; we estimate 2 sprints for the autoscaler rebuild work and e2e tests. We plan a staged rollout with canary gates and regression checks.

Q: Will this increase our costs (by reducing aggressive downscales)?
A: Short-term mitigations will modestly increase baseline capacity in affected pools; mid/long-term work focuses on smarter decisions that balance cost and availability (expect net-neutral or improved economics after tuning).

Q: Could this have been prevented earlier?
A: Yes — with better cache hotness metrics and a conservative safety floor in autoscaler rules. We lacked a simple metric that would have flagged risk of cold-cache thrash.

Q: Any change to SLAs/credits?
A: No SLA changes right now. For customers who were materially impacted we offered one-time credits via CS; we are reviewing policy language for clarity.

Operational TODOs (short checklist):
- [ ] Finalize RFC for autoscaler and get product sign-off (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Add per-shard cache-hotness metric to monitoring (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Add sticky-pin step to incident runbook + tabletop exercise (owner: Elliot)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing postmortem for public KB if necessary (owner: CS lead)
- [ ] Schedule chaos regression that simulates transient HCs and cache warmup (owner: eng-test)

Open questions / notes to self:
- Confirm exact list of impacted accounts from billing logs (need finance access).
- Decide whether to publish a short external postmortem or keep to customer notifications only. Lean: internal + impacted customers only for now.
- Confirm the rollback plan for the autoscaler rewrite — need SRE + infra sync.

Formatting/slide suggestions for the all-hands deck:
- Slide 1: 1-line headline + TL;DR (3 bullets)
- Slide 2: timeline visual (6-8 step timeline)
- Slide 3: root cause schematic (little diagram of scale loop + cache eviction)
- Slide 4: actions taken + next steps (3 columns: short/mid/long)
- Slide 5: Q&A common questions + where to find the postmortem

Quick draft email blurb (for exec to copy):
Subject: Brief update — operational incident on March 3 (resolved)
Body: Today we want to share a short update on an incident that affected inference latency in two regions on March 3. The core issue was an autoscaler behavior combined with cache warm-up churn. We stabilized the system the same day and have a plan to prevent recurrence. No customer data was exposed. Full notes and next steps are on Confluence (CONFLUENCE-OPS-2026-INCIDENT-1).

Final notes:
This doc is a scratchpad — expect edits. Need to coordinate with CS for final customer messaging and legal if we decide an external postmortem is published. Also want to run the speaking notes by the CEO for tone before all-hands.

-- Elliot
